subject: Political Science
textbooks: Indian Constitution at Work, Class XI (NCERT)
Additional reference material (annexure to the CBSE document)
notes: Part A (Indian Constitution at Work) carries 40 and Part B (Political Theory) 40; the document gives marks for groups of chapters, recorded as units. Unit codes are prefixed A and B.

Additional reference material (classroom use, not assessed in the board exam): electoral reforms; quasi and competitive federalism; constitution amendments; liberty vs freedom; dimensions of justice; human rights; multiculturalism.

units.name: Constitution: Why and How?; Rights in the Indian Constitution

chapters.name: Constitution: Why and How?
topics: Why we need a constitution: coordination and assurance, decision-making powers, limits on government, aspirations and goals, fundamental identity
Authority of a constitution: mode of promulgation, substantive provisions, balanced institutional design
Making of the Indian Constitution: Constituent Assembly composition, procedures, inheritance of the nationalist movement, institutional arrangements
Provisions adapted from constitutions of other countries
outcomes: Appreciate the need for a constitution
Understand the circumstances in which the Indian Constitution was drafted
Evaluate how constitutions govern the distribution of power
Analyse how constitutional provisions have worked in real political life

chapters.name: Rights in the Indian Constitution
topics: Importance of rights; Bill of Rights
Fundamental rights: equality, freedom, against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, constitutional remedies
Directive principles of state policy
Relationship between fundamental rights and directive principles
outcomes: Identify violations of the rights to equality and freedom
Justify reasonable restrictions on rights
Use freedom of expression to advocate for others' rights

chapters.name: Election and Representation
topics: Elections and democracy
First past the post and proportional representation; why India adopted FPTP
Reservation of constituencies
Free and fair elections: universal franchise, right to contest, independent Election Commission
Electoral reforms
outcomes: Identify types and methods of election
Think critically about stakeholders in free and fair elections
Demonstrate the role of the Election Commission
Compare election systems of different countries

chapters.name: Executive
topics: What an executive is; types of executive
Parliamentary executive in India: power and position of the President, discretionary powers
Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
Permanent executive: bureaucracy
outcomes: Compare parliamentary and presidential executives
Analyse the composition and functioning of the executive

chapters.name: Legislature
topics: Why we need a parliament and two houses: Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha
Powers of Parliament; special powers of Rajya Sabha
Law making
Parliamentary control of the executive
Parliamentary committees; self-regulation
outcomes: Describe the law-making process
Differentiate the powers of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
Analyse the role of parliamentary committees

chapters.name: Judiciary
topics: Independence of the judiciary; appointment and removal of judges
Structure of the judiciary
Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court: original, writ, appellate, advisory
Judicial activism
Judiciary and rights; judiciary and Parliament
outcomes: Identify what makes the judiciary independent
Compare jurisdictions
Analyse why the judiciary has become proactive and conflicts with Parliament over amendments

chapters.name: Federalism
topics: What federalism is; federalism in the Indian Constitution: division of powers
Federalism with a strong central government
Conflicts: centre-state relations, demands for autonomy, governors and President's rule, new states, interstate conflicts
Special provisions: Jammu and Kashmir
outcomes: Explain the features of a federation
Identify subjects on which the union and states legislate
Discuss provisions that led to a strong Centre

chapters.name: Local Governments
topics: Why local governments; growth of local government in India
73rd Amendment: three tier structure, elections, reservations, transfer of subjects, State Election Commissioners, State Finance Commission
74th Amendment
Implementation of the 73rd and 74th Amendments
outcomes: Understand the Panchayati Raj system and its significance
Justify the significance of the 73rd and 74th amendments
Examine the significance of decentralisation

units.name: Constitution as a Living Document; The Philosophy of the Constitution

chapters.name: Constitution as a Living Document
topics: Are constitutions static? How to amend the constitution
Why so many amendments: differing interpretations, political consensus, controversial amendments
Basic structure and evolution of the constitution
Contribution of the judiciary; maturity of political leadership
outcomes: Appreciate why the Constitution is called a living document
Know the major amendments and the controversies raised

chapters.name: The Philosophy of the Constitution
topics: Constitution as a means of democratic transformation
Why go back to the Constituent Assembly
Political philosophy: individual freedom, social justice, respect for diversity and minority rights, secularism, universal franchise, federalism, national identity
Procedural achievements; criticisms and limitations
outcomes: Appreciate the philosophical vision of the Constitution
Evaluate its strengths and limitations

chapters.name: Political Theory: An Introduction
topics: What politics is
What we study in political theory
Putting political theory into practice
Why study political theory
outcomes: Define politics and identify political principles
Appreciate the contribution of political thinkers

chapters.name: Freedom
topics: The ideal of freedom
Sources of constraints and why we need them
The harm principle
Negative and positive liberty
outcomes: Evaluate negative and positive liberty
Explain J.S. Mill's harm principle
Assess limits on freedom from social and economic structures

chapters.name: Equality
topics: Why equality matters: equality of opportunity; natural and social inequalities
Three dimensions of equality
Feminism, socialism
Promoting equality
outcomes: Assess how different ideologies perceive equality
Recognise ways to promote equality

chapters.name: Social Justice
topics: What justice is: equal treatment for equals, proportionate justice, special needs
Just distribution
John Rawls' theory of justice
Pursuing social justice; free markets versus state intervention
outcomes: Classify dimensions of justice
State Rawls' veil of ignorance
Appreciate government measures to secure social justice

chapters.name: Rights
topics: What rights are and where they come from
Legal rights and the state
Kinds of rights
Rights and responsibilities
outcomes: Explain why rights need legal sanction
Describe kinds of rights

chapters.name: Citizenship
topics: Full and equal membership; equal rights
Citizen and nation
Universal and global citizenship
outcomes: Explain the meaning of citizenship
Discuss solutions to citizenship issues

chapters.name: Nationalism
topics: Nations and nationalism: shared beliefs, history and identity
National self-determination
Nationalism and pluralism
outcomes: Assess the strengths and limitations of nationalism
Examine national self-determination

chapters.name: Secularism
topics: What secularism is; inter-religious and intra-religious domination
Secular state: western and Indian models
Criticisms of Indian secularism: western import and minoritism, interventionist, vote bank politics
outcomes: Differentiate inter- and intra-religious domination
Compare western and Indian models of secularism
